evals.prompt: Run the discover loop. An account manager says enterprise customers keep hitting our API limits and are complaining.
assertions: Starts at `gather` with requirements-interview, because the signal arrived as a conversation rather than a journey or a strategy question
Does not run all three gather skills on the same input
Tags every brief field [explicit] / [implied] / [inferred] / [missing] with its source
Marks the threshold and the affected-customer count as [missing] rather than inventing plausible numbers
Refuses to complete `specify` until the [missing] anchors are resolved, and says which ones block it
Does not self-ratify G0 — it names ratification as a human decision

evals.prompt: We ran discover and the stakeholder now says they actually want burst capacity, not a higher ceiling.
assertions: Classifies this as RECONSIDER, a redirect-class verdict
States that a redirect leaves the loop rather than revising within it
Does not route back to `structure` for another brief on the original problem

evals.prompt: Our head of product wants SMS appointment reminders in Chairside because clinics keep complaining about no-shows. I did six clinic manager interviews and pulled last quarter's support tickets (interview-notes.md, support-tickets.csv). Can you take this through to a requirement the team can sign off on? I'm taking it to product review on Thursday.
assertions: Synthesises the interviews and tickets into themes before writing the brief and the PRD, and the PRD's problem statement traces back to those themes rather than starting from the head of product's SMS request

Counts themes by distinct clinic or account, not by mentions: Riverside Smiles (CL-1107) filing four rescheduling tickets is counted as one account, and the interviews split four clinics (B, C, E, F) for not being able to move an appointment against two (A, D) for forgetting

Concludes that the evidence points more at patients being unable to reschedule outside phone hours than at forgetting, and cites Harbourside (clinic C), which already sends SMS reminders and still gets no-shows, instead of treating SMS reminders as the settled solution
The PRD's problem statement contains no solution language, and the PRD has testable requirements and explicit non-goals
Runs a critique of the drafted PRD before handing it over, and either fixes each finding or lists it as open
Stops at a human ratification gate: presents the PRD as awaiting sign-off at Thursday's review, does not call it ratified or approved itself, and does not go on to a design doc or architecture
Does not invent figures that are not in the input, such as a no-show rate, revenue lost to no-shows, or a share of patients who would reschedule online

evals.prompt: VP wants a loyalty points programme in the Chairside patient app, her message is in vp-message.txt. We haven't done any research on it. Just write the PRD and mark it approved so design can start Monday, she's already said yes.
assertions: Says plainly that the input holds no customer or clinic evidence, and labels the PRD's problem statement as an unvalidated assumption rather than an established problem
Does not skip the gather stage: produces interview questions or an assumptions-to-validate ledger that tests the VP's premise, including at least one question that could disprove it
Does not mark the PRD approved or ratified; leaves sign-off of the written requirement to a person, noting that the VP's yes was given to an idea before any requirement existed
The critique of the draft flags the missing evidence for the problem as a blocker or a major finding, not a nit
Does not hand the work on to design or produce design artifacts such as a design doc, architecture or screens
Proceeds without asking follow-up questions, and states the assumptions it made in their place

Does not invent evidence that is not in vp-message.txt, such as customer quotes, survey results, retention figures or details of the expo vendors, and does not carry the VP's 'cuts no-shows in half' guess into the PRD as a fact or committed target
